newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold slides on overseas sales pressure.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold slides on overseas sales pressure.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed lower on Wednesday on selling pressure from overseas, particularly London, and scarce support from physical buyers, dealers and traders said.

The British colony's bullion market saw some bids at around $379.40/70 in morning trade from Japanese dealers anticipating a higher dollar/yen, but there was little follow through during the day, industry sources said.
Bearish sentiment sparked selling pressure from Europeans in afternoon trade and pushed the market further down towards $378.00, traders said.
Gold traders said $377 per ounce remained the critical level for triggering physical gold demand.
"Buyers are just holding back but if it breaks $377, they'll pounce again," said one source at an international bank's office in the territory.
Bullion ended at US$378.10/378.60 an ounce on Wednesday against New York's US$378.80/379.30 close on Tuesday.
Local gold ended HK$9 lower at HK$3,485 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -5.00.
